overall_summary: Bitcoin is under clear pressure from ETF outflows, long liquidations, and a sharp risk-off move driven by Iran strike talk and oil spiking above one hundred dollars. Elevated yields near five percent and a firm dollar add headwinds, while eighty to eighty-two thousand support remains unconfirmed. The tone for crypto is cautious and defensive heading into the Fed and data-heavy week.
key_points: Heavy ETF outflows and long liquidations hit Bitcoin
Iran tensions and oil above $100 drive risk-off
Yields near 5% and firm DXY weigh on markets
Fed hold and key data keep uncertainty elevated

items.title: Bitcoin briefly breaks $80K, $815M liquidations hit longs
items.summary: Bitcoin slid as low as about $79,200 on Saturday before reclaiming the $80,000 level and trading near $80,800 to $81,000 on Sunday. Thin weekend liquidity fueled a cascade that liquidated more than $800 million in crypto positions, with longs taking the vast majority of the pain, including over $400 million in just four hours. Traders should care because the flush cleared a lot of leverage right before the Federal Reserve meeting, but support is still being tested and further downside magnets sit lower if $80K fails.
items.impact: Short-term volatility with cleaned leverage; $80K hold key for direction

items.title: Spot Bitcoin ETFs reverse with $773M two-day outflows
items.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs swung hard from hundreds of millions in inflows to $635 million in net outflows on October 22, followed by another roughly $138 million on October 23. BlackRock’s IBIT and Fidelity’s FBTC led the redemptions, wiping out most of the prior three-day inflow streak even as the five-day total stayed modestly positive. This matters because ETF flows have been a primary institutional bid; sustained outflows remove a key demand pillar heading into the Fed decision and higher oil prices.
items.impact: Weaker institutional demand pressure on spot price

items.title: Trump Iran strike talk and oil spike hit risk assets
items.summary: President Trump said U.S. strikes on Iran could come as soon as Sunday or a deal could be reached instead, while reports of embassy drawdowns and elevated Brent crude above $117 fueled inflation and risk-off fears. Bitcoin’s dip below $80,000 coincided with these headlines and the broader selloff in tech. Traders need to watch this because any escalation keeps pressure on risk assets and complicates the Fed’s path, while a de-escalation could reverse the weekend flush.
items.impact: Macro headwind raising volatility into Fed week

items.title: Arthur Hayes dumps $22M directional book, eyes lower prices
items.summary: BitMEX co-founder Arthur Hayes said he dumped Maelstrom’s entire directional crypto book, with on-chain trackers estimating about $22 million sold, mostly Ether plus Ethena, Uniswap and other tokens. He wrote that markets may need to go down to go up amid dicey macro and geopolitical conditions, and he is waiting for a clearer money-printing signal. This is notable because Hayes is a high-profile voice; his profit-taking and cautious stance can amplify short-term risk-off sentiment even if he remains structurally long Bitcoin longer term.
items.impact: Sentiment drag from prominent trader exit

items.title: Coinbase flags $75K risk if $80-82K support fails
items.summary: In its weekly review Coinbase noted fading corporate treasury demand for Bitcoin in the second half of the year and sticky inflation risks that raise the odds of further Fed tightening. Strategists see the $80,000 to $82,000 zone as critical confluence support tied to moving averages and ETF cost basis; a break could open a move toward $73,000 to $75,000. Traders should care because it frames the levels that matter after the weekend flush and underscores that institutional spot demand is no longer as one-sided as earlier in the cycle.
items.impact: Defines key downside levels ahead of Fed

items.title: Circle Gateway adds cirBTC for cross-chain Bitcoin balances
items.summary: Circle expanded its Gateway product so users and developers can hold unified balances of its wrapped Bitcoin token cirBTC alongside USDC and EURC, with fast cross-chain access after deposits finalize. cirBTC is backed one-to-one by Bitcoin held at a regulated Circle entity and is initially available on Arc and Ethereum. This is constructive infrastructure news that improves institutional and developer usability of Bitcoin on-chain, though it is unlikely to move price immediately compared with flows and macro.
items.impact: Positive longer-term liquidity and utility for BTC wrappers

items.title: Fed Widely Expected to Hold Rates Wednesday
items.summary: Markets price roughly 90 percent odds the Federal Reserve holds the funds rate in the 3.75 to 4.00 percent range at this week's FOMC meeting ending Wednesday, with Chair Kevin Warsh holding a press conference. Economists largely expect a skip due to midterm elections proximity even as sticky inflation and high oil keep December hike odds elevated around 70-80 percent. Traders should care because any hawkish tone or updated guidance could reprice rate paths and hit risk assets including Bitcoin hard.
items.impact: Priced-in hold; guidance on December path key volatility driver

items.title: Oil Surges Above $100 on Middle East Supply Fears
items.summary: Brent crude settled near 117 dollars and WTI above 103 dollars on Friday, multi-month highs, after Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and a UAE oil spill raised supply disruption risks. The weekly gains add to already elevated energy costs that have been driving headline inflation higher. Crypto traders need to watch this because sustained high oil feeds sticky inflation, supports higher-for-longer rates, and typically pressures risk assets.
items.impact: Inflationary pressure raises odds of tighter Fed policy ahead

items.title: 10-Year Yield Hovers Near 5 Percent, DXY Firm
items.summary: The US 10-year Treasury yield ended the week around 5 percent after a sharp Thursday drop on AI-related risk-off flows then a partial rebound Friday, while the dollar index held firm near 102. Firm long-end yields and a resilient greenback reflect ongoing inflation and growth concerns despite softer near-term hike odds. This matters for traders as elevated real yields and a strong dollar remain classic headwinds for Bitcoin and other risk assets.
items.impact: Higher yields and strong dollar pressure risk assets

items.title: Q3 GDP and September PCE Due Thursday
items.summary: The advance Q3 GDP estimate and September personal income and outlays including core PCE inflation drop Thursday morning right after the Fed decision. Atlanta Fed GDPNow recently tracked around 3.5 percent growth while core PCE is expected near 3.1 percent year-over-year, still well above target. These prints will shape whether the Fed can stay patient or needs to lean more hawkish into year-end, directly affecting rate expectations and crypto liquidity conditions.
items.impact: Data will confirm or challenge post-FOMC rate path pricing

items.title: Multiple Central Banks Decide This Week
items.summary: Besides the Fed, the Bank of Canada and Reserve Bank of New Zealand are expected to hike 25 basis points on Wednesday while the ECB on Thursday and Bank of Japan on Friday are priced to hold. Guidance from Lagarde and Ueda on December moves will matter globally. Coordinated or divergent central bank signals can drive dollar moves, cross-asset volatility, and capital flows that spill into crypto markets.
items.impact: Global rate differentials and dollar direction in focus

items.title: Labor Market Still Resilient Ahead of Key Week
items.summary: Initial jobless claims recently printed at a three-month low near 194,000 with the four-week average also subdued, pointing to a still-tight labor market. Combined with solid GDP tracking this reduces odds of any near-term Fed easing and keeps the door open for further tightening later. Crypto traders should note that a hot labor backdrop plus oil-driven inflation leaves little room for dovish surprises this week.

items.title: Trump Teases Possible Iran Strike Sunday or Major Deal
items.summary: President Trump told reporters the US could launch another strike on Iran as soon as Sunday, while leaving open a big diplomatic agreement. This comes amid the eight-month US-Israel war with Iran that has already disrupted the Strait of Hormuz and driven oil higher. Traders should watch closely because any confirmed escalation would spike energy prices and trigger broad risk-off moves across equities and crypto, while a deal could reverse that premium.
items.impact: Heightened war risk premium on oil and risk assets

items.title: US Intel: Iran in Advanced Stages of Plots to Kill Americans
items.summary: A declassified memo from the Director of National Intelligence warns that Iran has ramped up lethal plots against US personnel to advanced stages in the Middle East and elsewhere. This prompted further drawdowns of diplomats and families from several regional embassies. For markets it raises the odds of retaliatory US or Israeli action and keeps the geopolitical risk premium elevated heading into US midterms.
items.impact: Elevates chance of broader Middle East military response

items.title: Brazil Votes in Knife-Edge Presidential Runoff Today
items.summary: Brazilians head to the polls Sunday in a runoff between incumbent leftist Lula da Silva and right-wing Flavio Bolsonaro, son of the former president and a Trump ally. Polls show a dead heat after Bolsonaro led the first round. The outcome matters for crypto and commodities traders because Brazil is a major emerging-market economy, iron ore and agricultural exporter, and any sharp political shift could move the real, soy, and risk sentiment across Latin America.
items.impact: Binary political outcome for EM assets and commodities

items.title: Houthis Launch Fresh Attacks on Saudi Oil Infrastructure
items.summary: Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis claimed strikes on multiple Saudi Aramco facilities, pipelines, refineries and airports, with the Saudi coalition reporting interceptions. Oil prices have already surged to multi-month highs on Middle East supply fears. Crypto traders care because sustained attacks on Saudi energy raise the global oil risk premium, feed inflation worries and typically pressure risk assets including Bitcoin.
items.impact: Sustains high oil prices and energy-driven risk-off pressure

items.title: Ukraine Starlink Speeds Restored After Musk Throttling
items.summary: Ukrainian officials confirmed Starlink and military Starshield connections returned to full high speeds after more than a week of restrictions that hampered drone operations. Elon Musk said SpaceX limited the commercial service because Ukraine used it for offensive strikes, while Trump reportedly pressed for restoration. This stabilizes Ukraine's frontline capabilities in the ongoing war and removes one near-term source of operational friction that markets had been watching.
items.impact: Removes short-term drag on Ukrainian military effectiveness

items.title: Hundreds of Thousands Protest Across France Against Macron
items.summary: Over 400,000 people marched across France on Saturday against living costs, school conditions and inequality, with clashes, tear gas and nearly 1,000 arrests in Paris and other cities. The unrest, partly fueled by energy price spikes from Middle East conflicts, challenges President Macron in his final months. European political instability of this scale can weigh on the euro and broader risk sentiment if it escalates further toward the 2027 election.
items.impact: Adds European political risk premium amid energy-driven discontent
